questions.questionText: Why does a metal spoon feel colder than a wooden spoon when both are kept in the same room?
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat much better than wood, so it draws heat away from your hand faster, making it feel colder.

options.text: Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster

questions.questionText: If an object is moving at a constant speed in a straight line, what is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. Constant speed in a straight line means velocity is unchanged, so acceleration is zero.

questions.questionText: Which of the following has the highest electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Among these materials, rubber is a good electrical insulator and has very high resistance.

questions.questionText: Why do astronauts appear weightless while orbiting Earth?
questions.explanation: Astronauts and their spacecraft are continuously falling around Earth together. This continuous free fall creates the sensation of weightlessness.

options.text: There is no gravity in space
They and their spacecraft are in continuous free fall

questions.questionText: What happens to the boiling point of water at a high altitude?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases at higher altitudes, lowering the temperature at which water boils.

options.text: Water cannot boil at high altitudes

questions.questionText: Which colour of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum, while red has the longest.

questions.questionText: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.explanation: Potassium's symbol is K, derived from its Latin name, Kalium.

questions.questionText: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.explanation: At 25°C, a neutral aqueous solution has a pH of 7.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a chemical change rather than a physical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting produces new substances, mainly hydrated iron oxides, so it is a chemical change.

questions.questionText: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one proton in its nucleus, giving it atomic number 1.

questions.questionText: Which blood cells are primarily responsible for fighting infections?
questions.explanation: White blood cells, also called leukocytes, are key components of the immune system.

questions.questionText: Which layer of Earth's atmosphere contains most of the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, where it absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.questionText: Why does lightning appear before thunder is heard?
questions.explanation: Light travels vastly faster than sound, so the flash reaches us before the sound of thunder.

options.text: Thunder is produced several seconds later
Lightning occurs at a higher temperature

questions.questionText: Which phenomenon explains why a straw appears bent when placed in a glass of water?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes between materials with different refractive indices, such as air and water.

questions.questionText: A car travels 150 kilometres in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h.

questions.questionText: Which gas makes up the largest percentage of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of dry air, making it the most abundant atmospheric gas.

questions.questionText: Which vitamin can the human body produce in the skin when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet B radiation helps the skin produce vitamin D3.

questions.questionText: Which type of energy is stored in a stretched spring?
questions.explanation: A stretched or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy.

questions.questionText: What is the boiling point of the water?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100° C at sea level.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of an enzyme in the human body?
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions by lowering their activation energy.

options.text: To slow down all chemical reactions
To speed up specific chemical reactions

questions.questionText: Which sub-atomic particle has a negative electric charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons carry a negative charge, protons carry a positive charge, and neutrons have no electric charge.

questions.questionText: Which process allows green plants to convert light energy into chemical energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to help convert carbon dioxide and water into sugars, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

questions.questionText: What happens to the electrical current in a simple series circuit if one bulb is removed and the circuit is left open?
questions.explanation: An open circuit breaks the conducting path, so current stops flowing throughout the series circuit.

questions.questionText: Which of these substances is an element rather than a compound?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas (O₂) consists only of oxygen atoms. Water and carbon dioxide are compounds, while air is a mixture.

questions.questionText: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster than an ordinary open pot?
questions.explanation: Higher pressure raises the boiling point of water, allowing the food to cook at a higher temperature.

options.text: It reduces the boiling point of water
It raises the boiling point of water
It removes all oxygen from food
It increases the amount of water in food

questions.questionText: Which force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun's gravitational attraction provides the centripetal acceleration that keeps planets in their orbits.

questions.questionText: Which of these is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is naturally replenished by the Sun, unlike fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum.

questions.questionText: Why do water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass?
questions.explanation: Water vapour in the surrounding air cools when it touches the cold glass and condenses into liquid droplets. This process is called condensation.

options.text: Water vapour in the air condenses on the glass
The glass produces water when cooled
The cold glass absorbs liquid water from the air

questions.questionText: Why does a pressure cooker whistle when it is cooking?
questions.explanation: Steam escaping through the pressure regulator causes it to vibrate, producing the familiar whistle. The regulator helps control the pressure inside the cooker.

options.text: Escaping steam makes the pressure regulator vibrate
The metal expands and produces sound by itself
Food releases trapped air that creates the whistle

questions.questionText: Why does a wet cloth dry faster on a windy day?
questions.explanation: Wind carries away the humid air surrounding the cloth, allowing more water to evaporate. This generally speeds up drying.

options.text: Wind increases the boiling point of water
Wind removes moist air near the cloth, helping evaporation
Wind makes the cloth absorb water

questions.questionText: All acids contain oxygen.
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is an acid that contains no oxygen.

questions.questionText: Pure water is a good conductor of electricity.
questions.explanation: Pure water is a very poor conductor. The ions dissolved in ordinary water are mainly responsible for its electrical conductivity.

questions.questionText: The mass of an object changes when it is taken from Earth to the Moon.
questions.explanation: Mass remains the same. Weight changes because the Moon's gravitational acceleration is weaker than Earth's. Weight = Mass x Gravity

questions.questionText: Carbon dioxide is used by plants during photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide and water to produce sugars during photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: The nucleus of an atom contains protons and neutrons.
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains positively charged protons and electrically neutral neutrons, except that ordinary hydrogen-1 has no neutron.

questions.questionText: The ozone layer protects Earth by absorbing much of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone absorbs much of the harmful ultraviolet radiation reaching Earth.
